Strategy.approach: Artifact integrity first: parseability → cross-link coherence → deterministic projection and routing → macro/governance correctness → bootstrap fit → workspace boundary fit.
Strategy.mocking-policy: Prefer deterministic artifact checks and explicit review criteria over speculative prose tests.
Strategy.coverage-target: 100% of canonical VIBE surfaces parse cleanly and cross-reference the same contract story.

contract.purpose: Verify that framework identity, principles, and the optional role of vibestart are stated coherently.

scenarios.scenario-1: VIBE is described as a standalone methodology.
scenarios.scenario-2: vibestart is described as optional, not mandatory.
scenarios.scenario-3: Core principles do not contradict the artifact model.
scenarios.scenario-4: If docs/technology.xml exists, it remains a GRACE compatibility shim and does not redefine canonical VIBE core semantics.

traces.trace-1: CrossLinks from identity decisions to the framework and product nodes remain valid.

TracePolicy.deterministic-first: Prefer stable fields and exact assertions over prose-heavy logs.
TracePolicy.redaction: Never log secrets, credentials, raw high-risk payloads, or hidden reasoning.

BranchVisibility.rule-1: Every critical route choice must be reconstructable from explicit routing fields.
BranchVisibility.rule-2: Every governance escalation must expose the triggering signals and final selected review floor.
BranchVisibility.rule-3: Every sync run must expose reconcile and cleanup phases separately when both occur.
BranchVisibility.rule-4: Every bootstrap run must expose explicit profile selection and the first-run contract fields.

module-level.purpose: Fast deterministic checks against one module contract or one tightly bounded artifact surface.
module-level.typical-checks: XML parse, TOML parse, field assertions, guard assertions, and local cross-reference checks.

wave-level.purpose: Checks only the merged surfaces touched by a bounded execution wave.
wave-level.typical-checks: Cross-artifact coherence, targeted refresh, reconcile-only sync verification, and scoped trace assertions.

phase-level.purpose: Broader integrity checks before a planning or implementation phase is considered complete.
phase-level.typical-checks: Phase gates, cross-link integrity, compatibility boundary checks, and broader review audits.

ExecutionReadiness.summary: Current repository surfaces are planning artifacts and shared canonical documents. They are suitable for guided single-agent work and unsuitable for parallel worker ownership because the write scopes overlap heavily.

module.reason: Identity surfaces are canonical shared artifacts and must not be edited concurrently.
Ontology and projection invariants are foundational shared truth and need tightly reviewed sequential edits.
Macro contracts define public semantics; experimental auto behavior exists but is not yet normative.
Governance policy is a shared control surface and should not be mutated by parallel workers.
Configuration boundary and defaults are shared and drift-sensitive.
Bootstrap contract is a shared product surface; profile semantics must remain globally coherent.
Workspace boundary and release-surface policy are shared repo-level contracts and should change only through deliberate sequential edits.
The active bootstrap entrypoint writes shared root surfaces and must remain deterministic and sequential until richer product adapters exist.
Beta boundary and operator guidance are shared adoption surfaces and should remain globally coherent.
The git acquisition wrapper is a shared entrypoint and must keep source, ref, and target path semantics deterministic.
